pages.lesson:
LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.1 Pythagorean Relationship (4 lessons) Relationship of the sides 
Topic 3.2: Length

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Length. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we use different units of measuring length?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform operations involving units of length in different situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Length.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Length using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Communication and Collaboration: as the learner works with peers when measuring the lengths of various objects and also as they discuss the relationship between circumference and diameter.
2. Self-efficacy: as the learner practices different operations using length.
3. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner relates circumference to diameter. Values
4. Integrity: as the learner carries out the activities and gives the correct measurement.
5. Unity: as the learner works together in measuring the lengths of various objects. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs)

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we use different units of measuring length?
2. How do we measure the perimeter of different objects?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Length is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
